decisionsSentToArchitect: R6: a body of several references keeps a card per reference (today's margin) and gains them in the Inbox and Conversation, rather than the margin narrowing to one reference
A linked bare key reads 'KEY title' and a #id reads as its question's text, per R4
A key naming the text's own issue is indexed and linked, as dispatch://<own key> is today
Overlap with INFRA-156 in text/, refs/, docs/ excerpts and triggers; whichever merges second rebases

findings.finding: A #id can be indexed before its question's ask row exists (settlement makes rows after the version is indexed, one at a time), and nothing re-indexes it.
findings.answer: Decision 7: every ask row gaining a block_id (either build, by trigger) and every document version enqueue a scope item; draining it re-indexes each source in ScopeSources(doc) whose text holds a # candidate. #id resolves against the question map of the document's latest text (decision 5), not retracted rows of removed blocks.

findings.finding: Old-text plan hazards: triggers double-index new writes; backfill in a migration vs code; an older build's excerpt pass could pin empty excerpts on new edges; backfilled edges have no source_seq and deploy-time created_at.
findings.answer: Decision 8: ReplaceCounted deletes its own source's refs_owed row in the write's transaction; seed is the last migration after the triggers, writing only the new table (~4,600 rows); the drain cuts document excerpts in the same transaction so no owed excerpt is left for an older build; backfilled edges take the source's write time, no source_seq or event as rebuild-refs; one trigger per migration with census.

findings.finding: text.ExtractAt has other callers (references route query parser, MentionExcerpts) without a resolver.
findings.answer: Decision 9: Extract/ExtractAt unchanged; new text.Mentions(body, serverURL, Resolver); refs.targets and MentionExcerpts take the resolver.

findings.finding: Boundary rules contradict A1 (backtick), leave ~, |,  , link destinations, the right end and the #id charset/trim open.
findings.answer: Decisions 1-4 settle each, with table rows in Task 1; the backtick, ~, | and numeric whitespace additions are recorded as a spec departure (outcome unchanged).

findings.finding: Renderers do not know which text they draw; #id scope depends on it; ~35 call sites.
findings.answer: Decision 13: optional source {kind,id} prop, each call site listed with its source or 'keys only'; scope computed server-side by GET /api/v1/references/questions (decision 12).

findings.finding: Existence checks cost: getIssue per key with 404 retries; agent text full of UTF-8-like tokens; scope lookups; copied-block parsing on writes; locking loader.
findings.answer: Web: one cached getIssue per distinct key with 404 final in the reference queries' own options; scope query only for bodies with a # candidate. Server: one key = any($1) select only when a candidate exists; question map only when a # candidate exists, plain selects and a directive-line scan, never loadAskBlocks.

findings.finding: R4 open parts: missing vs loading, issue title format, whether a linked key/#id shows text or title.
findings.answer: Decision 10: 404 final; missing or loading shows the written text; issue reads key then title (IssueList convention); linked key and #id show the target's title per R4, sent to the architect.

findings.finding: R6 'one reference' vs today's multi-reference margin cards; unnamed surfaces; composer chips share composerReferences.

specDepartures.spec: Design 1: a key counts only when the character before it is the start of the text, whitespace, or one of ( [ " ' * _ >.
specDepartures.plan:
Also a backtick, ~, |, and a numeric character reference for whitespace ( ,  , 	, 
) immediately before the key.
specDepartures.evidence: A1 requires every positive row inside a code span to be indexed by the server, which a backtick before the key forbids under Design 1's list; refs.go:13-22 ends a reference at | for a table cell and trims ~ for strikethrough; stored markdown writes a mark's edge space as   (pmdoc/escape.go:131-157).

specDepartures.spec: R6: a reply or message whose whole text is one reference shows the card; text with anything else beside the reference shows no card.
specDepartures.plan: A body made only of references (one or more, whitespace-separated) shows one card per reference on the margin, the Inbox reply and the Conversation, as the margin does today; any other text beside them shows none.
specDepartures.evidence: Unfurl.tsx:90-99 and Unfurl.test.tsx:322-331: the margin cards several bare references today; reading R6 as a narrowing would remove that from the margin, which no requirement asks for. A7's cases hold as written.
